newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo silver and palladium futures slump.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo silver and palladium futures slump.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly lower on Friday with both benchmark silver and palladium futures hitting their life-of-contract lows during the day, following New York falls, traders said.
Silver futures ranged from 2.9 yen to 4.8 yen per 10 grams lower. Benchmark silver ended 3.9 yen lower at 177.3 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from three yen per gram lower to two firmer, with benchmark August ending flat at 428 yen.
"Activity in silver futures was buoyant as private investors hunted for bargains," a trading house trader said.
Japanese trade houses sold silver futures while buying spot silver in arbitrage trade.

"Japanese trade houses were believed to have bought around 4.0 to 5.0 million ounces of spot silver. But the active buying failed to boost spot prices due to selling pressure from overseas especially at around $4.95 level," the trader said.
For palladium, late bargain-hunting was detected.
Traders said the downside in Tokyo precious metal futures are likely to be limited, buoyed by the yen's weaker tone.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to two yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was two yen lower at 1,335 yen.
Bullion was quoted at $382.35/2.65 per ounce at 0753 GMT, against $382.50/383.00 in New York on Thursday.
In gold futures, activity was mainly dominated by spread-trade by trade houses, as the participation of private investors was still limited, they said.
Platinum trading was featureless as the market continued to suffer from a lack of fresh incentives.
Platinum futures ranged from one to four yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was four yen lower at 1,359 yen.
